title.en: The morning the Chuo Line stopped

summary.en: A weekday morning. Rapid trains on the Chuo Line stop after an accident near Musashi-Koganei. Commuters at seven stations decide: wait, detour, take a taxi, or give up.
summary.ja: 平日の朝、武蔵小金井付近の人身事故で中央線快速が止まる。7 つの駅の通勤客が「待つ・迂回する・タクシーに乗る・あきらめる」を決める。

scenario.en: The Chuo Line rapid service stops for about an hour on a weekday morning after an accident. Simulate commuters at the stations between Tachikawa and Nakano heading for central Tokyo. Do they wait, use another line, take a taxi, or give up? Show how crowds, detour queues and taxi queues build up, and what better information or more detour capacity would change.
scenario.ja: 平日の朝、人身事故で中央線快速が 1 時間ほど止まる。立川から中野までの駅から都心へ向かう通勤客をシミュレートしてほしい。待つのか、別の路線を使うのか、タクシーに乗るのか、あきらめるのか。ホームの混雑、迂回の行列、タクシーの行列がどう伸びるか、正確な案内や振替輸送の増強で何が変わるかを見たい。

questions.en: How many people wait, and how many switch to a detour or a taxi?
questions.ja: 何人が待ち、何人が迂回やタクシーに切り替えるか。

questions.en: Does an accurate early estimate of the restart time reduce the total delay?
questions.ja: 再開時刻を早く正確に知らせると、全体の遅れは減るか。

questions.en: Which station suffers most, and why?
questions.ja: どの駅が一番苦しくなるか。その理由は何か。

assumptions.en: All numbers (commuter counts, capacities, fares, travel times) are assumptions, not measured data.
assumptions.ja: 通勤客の数、輸送力、運賃、所要時間は、すべて仮定の値で、実測ではない。

assumptions.en: People are modelled as 28 cohorts (7 stations x 4 types) plus 3 named individuals.
assumptions.ja: 人は 28 の集団（7 駅 × 4 タイプ）と、名前のある 3 人で表す。

assumptions.en: Without AI, each cohort splits by a logit choice model over time and money cost.
assumptions.ja: AI なしのとき、各集団は時間とお金のコストによるロジット選択モデルで分かれる。

agents.persona: Office and shop workers who must be at work by 9:00. Being late is embarrassing and noticed. Careful with money but will pay to avoid a serious lateness. Cannot work from home.

name.ja: フレックス・在宅可の会社員

agents.persona: Workers with flexible hours; about half can work from home. They hate crowds and wasted time more than being late. They check their phones for information constantly.
High school and university students. Very little money, so taxis are almost never an option. A delay certificate excuses lateness, but some have a test or a presentation today.
Older people going to hospital appointments, and people with errands. Less comfortable with complicated transfers and packed trains. An appointment can often be moved by phone.
Kenji, 38, sales manager living in Kokubunji, heading to Yotsuya. He has an important client meeting at 9:30 that he set up himself. Hates being late, would pay for a taxi if it clearly helps.
Mika, 20, university student from Kichijoji. She has an exam at 9:00 that cannot be retaken easily. She has 2,000 yen in her wallet and a commuter pass for the Chuo Line only.

name.ja: サトウ（45 歳・エンジニア）
